exact_statement: For every finite uniform-cube Boolean sign f and distinct physical coordinates i,j, let C_i,C_j,C_ij be the weighted squared-density row collisions and O_k=Inf_k-beta_k the singleton excess orientation energies. For Fourier quartets (alpha,beta,gamma,delta), q=sum amplitudes squared, define P_ij=sum_t 4(alpha delta+beta gamma)^2/q, M_i=sum_t[4alpha^2 beta^2/(alpha^2+beta^2)+4gamma^2 delta^2/(gamma^2+delta^2)-4(alpha beta+gamma delta)^2/q], and M_j analogously interchanging beta,gamma. Zero-mass fractions are zero. Then M_i,M_j>=0 and C_ij=C_i+C_j+P_ij-M_i-M_j exactly; P_ij<=2(Inf_i+Inf_j), and C_ij<=2(C_i+C_j)+2(O_i+O_j). On a least-essential-dimension FEI(K) violating witness, K>0, deficit D>0 and actual singleton child reserves S_i,S_j>=0, the reviewed scalar bound r_K=log2(1+2^(2/ln2-K)) yields C_ij<=2(C_i+C_j)+(2/K)(2r_K-2D-S_i-S_j). The unconditional singleton-only bound is still false on the exact three-bit parity guard. The orientation coefficient2 is sharp for arbitrary real quartets, not claimed sharp for Boolean functions. For K>=4, the displayed bound can substitute into the reviewed two-bit phase-bank upper bound by monotonicity, but supplies no pair-selection theorem or universal FEI constant.
